I'm playing Age of Wonders 3, I can't get past the first dragon-people mission because they expect you to take on two empires twice your size from basically zero.

I'm looking for a game where it's easy for both the AI and the player to make mistakes. I really hate how the AI only attacks when it has a clear advantage, and it's only worth attacking when you'll completely, one-sidedly decimate the enemy. I want something where I don't have to have to waste turns because my units have to catch up. I want something where it's actually worth it to make risky moves.
Looking for a 4x game for someone impatient and hates micromanagement.

Well, I'm not sure I can relate to your issues with Age of Wonders 3.

But I've really enjoyed Endless Legend and Endless Space. Endless Legend especially has less micromanagement though. The world is broken into regions, and each region can only support one city. You won't get any infinite city sprawls in this game. Combat can also be tactical, where your army will actually move around, fight and use special abilities on the world map once battle is engaged. I tend to find I only have 3 or 4 active armies at a time in that game.

Also, every race in that game plays wildly different. One is only allowed to have a single city, and when they conquer other people, all their citizens are sent back to that one enormous city. One can only heal by spending money. One of them has complete control over the international markets and can lock people out. They got really creative with some of them.

Some people have complained however that the tech tree isn't very good, and IMHO it's the weakest part of the game.

I feel your pain on AoW. It's a really fun game but I had similar troubles. I got through the first map or two and thought I understood things. Then I got to a point where I was just getting ramped up and the AI showed up with a gigantic army in a way I didn't even know they could and stomped me. I haven't gotten around to returning to it since.

There's a freeware title called 10-Minute Space Strategy that might work. It's incredibly simple as far as 4X games are concerned, but it has no government or diplomacy to worry about. The translation isn't great, though, but the mechanics become clear after a couple playthroughs.
